title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n10 = 1, n01 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, failure diagnosis, artifact-grounded reproducibility guidance, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness in such workflows depends on produced configurations satisfying deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering/workflow constraints, and safety group constraints). While prior work has prototyped intent→configuration translation and suggested verifier-integrated generator pipelines, there is limited artifact-grounded evidence quantifying how verifier-based guardrails change deterministic-invariant compliance under a tightly controlled experimental design [1],[2].

This study asks the following preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The paired design isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair (a repair-only effect) rather than effects from constrained prompting or independent multi-sample strategies.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) that executed 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis: baseline pass 199/200, guarded pass 200/200, contingency table (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis: the single repaired case involved a multi-device ordering violation that the repair corrected deterministically. (5) A bounded interpretation of implications, reproducibility notes, and threats to validity consistent with the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps research has explored intent-driven configuration synthesis, prototype evaluation pipelines, and the role of validation or verification stages in reducing hazardous outputs [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain generate→validate→repair patterns (program repair, decompilation, RAG/Tool-augmented agents) motivate guarded pipelines as a practical design pattern, but empirical demonstrations in NetOps with verifier-grounded acceptance metrics are sparse in the surveyed literature [4],[5]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM safety highlight common failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and recommend verifier gates and provenance recording for operational workflows [6],[7].

Relation to our study. Unlike prior multi-model benchmark work that reports aggregate accuracy on curated question banks, our contribution is a tightly scoped, preregistered measurement of the repair-only effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. This isolates how allowing a single verifier-triggered repair alters verifier acceptance of the identical initial candidate, a narrower estimand than independent first-pass comparisons or multi-sample prompting studies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study CAND-2026-001 prior to observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, computed as the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), allowed at most one automated repair call per task, and declared a single confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The full preregistration text and SHA-256 are archived in the execution bundle.

Task bank and deterministic sampling. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce 200 tasks drawn from very_hard and extreme workflow patterns (multi-device ordering constraints and dependency rules). The sampling rule was fixed in preregistration: for zero-based ordinal j in 0..199, task_index = 8*cycle + offset per the preregistered deterministic mapping; inclusion and exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks, syntactic pre-checks) were applied before any model calls. No preregistered exclusions occurred. Each task manifest encodes an initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies; representative task manifests and the deterministic task generator version are archived (see task_manifest.jsonl and representative task entries).

Model calls, generation semantics, and model configuration. Per the preregistration and execution manifest, the hosted model declared was gpt-5-mini and execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). The manifest records model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair). We explicitly record that temperature = null is an archived metadata field and is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling remains possible. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implemented the shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial sample deterministically reused by both conditions) and enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rules. The binary outcome per task was computed by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The verifier pipeline applied deterministic syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, required_sequence (encoded ordering constraints), group-level invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules present in each task manifest. The verifier returns detailed validator traces per episode (validation_before/validation_after), violation codes, and a final boolean valid flag. The scoring rule used for the confirmatory estimand was full_intent_constraint_validation: score = 1 if all required invariants pass, else 0. Validator traces and scoring artifacts for every episode are archived (execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/).
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records: started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call audit stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1; hosted_model_call_event_count = 201.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv):

- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.

Contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): guarded × baseline counts: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Statistical inference. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar implementation (analysis executor: exact_mcnemar_two_sided). Conceptually the test enumerates the binomial distribution of discordant outcomes (n = n10 + n01) under the null that discordant outcomes are equally likely; the two-sided p-value sums the tail probabilities of observing discordant counts at least as extreme as the observed outcome. For observed discordants n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 (n = 1), the exact two-sided McNemar p reported by the analysis executor is 1.0 (analysis artifact: analysis/results.json). We also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference using 10,000 resamples with seed 1729, yielding [0.00, 0.015] (artifact: analysis_log.jsonl and paired_difference_figure.svg). These exact numbers and bootstrap parameters are archived.

Repair activity and failure diagnosis. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair for one task (provider-call audit: repair = 1). The archived validator_trace for that task shows the baseline candidate failed due to a multi-step ordering/workflow violation with respect to the task's required_sequence; the repair produced an adjusted command sequence that satisfied the ordering constraints and was accepted by the verifier. Representative per-task artifacts (responses and scoring traces) for this repaired pair are available at execution/responses/task-000008-* and execution/scoring/task-000008-*. Example shared-initial and guarded-final normalized configurations (artifact SHA-256s are archived) and the validator's before/after snapshots appear in the archived scoring JSON for the specific pair.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to the preregistered estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the paired comparison isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair on the identical initial candidate; it does not measure effects of specialized guarded prompts, constrained generation strategies, or independent first-pass generations per condition. Claims about constrained prompting or multi-sample advantages therefore require a different preregistered execution semantics and are outside the scope of this report.

Statistical and power considerations. The preregistration's power plan targeted detection of ~10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 under mid-range baseline pass assumptions (~45–65%). The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) substantially exceeded planning assumptions, reducing realized power to detect small absolute improvements. The single repaired case produced an absolute increase of 0.5 percentage points; the discrete nature of discordant counts (n=1) leads to the exact McNemar p = 1.0 for a two-sided test. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) provides a quantified interval for the possible true paired difference under resampling consistent with the observed data.

Failure-mode implications and operational intuition. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach—consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device policy interactions and ordered workflows concentrate failure risk. In this artifact-grounded run the verifier gate plus a single repair sufficed to correct that localized ordering fault. This suggests guarded repair is effective when failures are sequence-conformance or reordering faults that a repair prompt can deterministically correct; it does not imply general effectiveness for other fault classes (e.g., semantic misinterpretation of intent, missing dependencies observable only in live telemetry).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics, single initial generation per task, and no independent first-pass contrasts. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces syntactic, workflow, and selected network-level invariants encoded per task manifest, but it does not emulate live-device telemetry or executed dataplane behaviors. External validity: synthetic deterministic task bank, single model (gpt-5-mini), and absence of adversarial contamination testing limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: the rare discordant-pair count implies large sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects; the bootstrap CI and exact-test p-value reflect this discrete regime.

Reproducibility guidance grounded in artifacts. The execution bundle archives: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/scoring/, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, and the deterministic_reconciliation.json. Key numeric values reported here (baseline_success_count = 199, guarded_success_count = 200, model_calls_used = 201, bootstrap_seed = 1729, bootstrap_resamples = 10000) exactly match the archived artifacts. The initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is reported in the Disclosure Statement. Researchers can replicate the confirmatory analysis by rerunning the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl as indexed in execution/execution_manifest.json; the analysis artifacts include machine-verifiable hashes.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-produced network configurations. In this synthetic, deterministic task set with gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.015]); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 given one discordant pair. The artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can fix localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require multi-model evaluation, independent first-pass contrasts if those estimands are desired, adversarial contamination testing, larger and more diverse task banks, and live-device validation. All artifacts and analysis outputs supporting these claims are archived with the execution manifest and hashes provided in the execution bundle.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the manifest indexing archived artifact paths). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock; humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
